issue: On a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS APFS, where /rails-flow:fix and /rails-flow:feature run the gate at merge), a record r.md with 'Mock-up: docs/product/mockups/R.md' passes with no problems. resolve() keeps the case as written, so the equality fails, then is_file() is True and the RECORD_DIR prefix passes. Reproduced: record_problems returned []. The CHANGELOG says a record cannot name itself. Fix: (root/mock).exists() and (root/mock).samefile(path). Add R.md as a selftest case and a mutation.

a.md names b.md and b.md names a.md: both pass, and neither shows a mock-up. The new CONTROL treats a record naming another record as correct. Fix: refuse a Mock-up that is itself a record (a .md under RECORD_DIR), or follow the chain.

'    - mockup-gate: off' (4+ spaces, top level) is a CommonMark indented code block, so it is an example, yet OPT_OUT's ^\s* counts it as the declaration. This predates the PR but is the same fence class. Fix: ^ {0,3} in OPT_OUT, or drop indented-code lines in unfenced().

In CommonMark a backtick fence's info string cannot contain a backtick, so '``` a`b' is not a fence. unfenced() treats it as one and hides a real opt-out after it. This fails closed: the gate stays on. Fix: for a backtick opener, reject a backtick in the rest of the line.

A record path in backticks, or as a markdown link target [r](docs/product/mockups/bell.md), is not seen as linked, because the pattern needs ^ or \s before it. This predates the PR and fails closed. It reaches check_slices.verdict too. Fix: (?:^|[\s(`\[]) before the path.

The trailing \b accepts 'docs/product/mockups/bell.md-draft' and 'docs/product/mockups/foo.pdf.TBD' as linked, so the extension rule is only partly enforced. Fix: end with (?=[\s.,;:)`]*(?:\s|$)), and add a case with a control.

The new (?![\w/-]|\.\w) lookahead refuses app/views/bell.html.erb outside docs/product/mockups/. dev linked it, and PR #1478's ledger names .html.erb as a real mock-up. The CHANGELOG does not disclose this. Fix: allow a known template suffix, e.g. (?:\.erb)?, add a fixture.

lstrip(" ") counts a tab as indent 0, so 'Example:\n\n\t- mockup-gate: off' (an indented code block in CommonMark) still turns the gate off, failing open. Fix: measure line.expandtabs(4), add a fixture.

A continuation line in a list item resets the list context. '- Gates:\n  more text\n    - mockup-gate: off' is a nested item. It declared off on dev and no longer does, which contradicts the CHANGELOG claim that it still counts under a list item. Fix: keep the list context across non-blank, non-list lines until a blank line is followed by a non-list line.
'- Gates:\n\n      mockup-gate: off' (content indent plus 4, which is a code block inside the item) still declares. The docstring and CHANGELOG say every 4+ indent under a list is a nested item.
The CHANGELOG says foo.pdf.TBD names nothing, but docs/product/mockups/foo.pdf.TBD is still linked (the record alternative accepts any extension). Scope the sentence to paths outside the folder.
There are no fixtures for tab indent, ordered lists (1. and 1)), + bullets, a lazy or continuation line, or a heading followed by indented code. R2 and R3 pass all 25 mutations.
OPT_OUT uses Unicode \s, so a line indented with NBSP (rendered as paragraph text) declares off. Pre-existing. Use [ \t].
Outside the folder, design/bell.gif and design/bell.avif are refused on the issue side but accepted by the gate. Pre-existing on dev.
The comment defers list-scoped fences to '#1461's shared scanner'. #1461 is CLOSED, and unindented_code is a new local scanner, not a shared one. Update the pointer or file the shared scanner.
